tools.name: scan_token
tools.description: Run a full DeFade scan on one token contract: token metadata, holder distribution, creator info and the headline risk verdict. Start here for any "is this token safe", "is this a rug pull" or "should I buy this" question. Returns risk.score as a SAFETY score where 100 is clean and low numbers are da

tools.name: get_rug_score
tools.description: Rug pull probability for one token: a 0-100 score where HIGHER MEANS MORE DANGEROUS, a verdict label, and the individual signals that drove it. This is the opposite direction from scan_token's safety score. Use it when the question is specifically about rug likelihood.

tools.name: get_holders
tools.description: Holder distribution for one token, with liquidity pools, burn addresses, lockers, exchange wallets and contracts classified out, so the top-holder list reflects actual holders. Use it to answer how concentrated the supply is and whether a few wallets could collapse the chart.

tools.name: get_whales
tools.description: Wallets large enough to move this token's price, and what they have been doing. Use it after get_holders when the question is about who can dump and whether they are already dumping.

tools.name: get_liquidity
tools.description: Liquidity pool analysis for one token, including burn and lock verification and pool depth. Use it to answer whether liquidity is locked, how deep it is, and whether the position could be pulled.

tools.name: get_bundles
tools.description: Coordinated buys bundled into the launch of one token — wallets that acquired supply together before the public could. Heavy bundling that is still held is one of the strongest rug predictors. For the deeper analysis with delayed sweeps and peak-net-exposure accounting, call get_bundles_pro.

tools.name: get_bundles_pro
tools.description: Deep bundle analysis for one token: the launch window plus delayed sweeps, accounted on peak net exposure rather than raw buy count, so wallets that bought and flipped are not counted as holders. Use when get_bundles flags something and you need the real still-held share.

tools.name: get_snipers
tools.description: Bots that bought in the first block or first seconds of this token's launch, and whether they are connected to the deployer. Use it to tell an organic launch from a pre-arranged one.

tools.name: get_insider_network
tools.description: The graph of wallets around one token that look independent but are linked by funding, transfers or timing — typically the deployer's supply fanned out to look like organic demand. Use it when the holder list looks distributed and you want to know whether it really is.

tools.name: get_smart_money
tools.description: Wallets with a track record of profitable entries that are holding or trading this token. Use it for the bullish side of a scan: who informed is in, and when they got in.

tools.name: get_dev_tracker
tools.description: What the token's creator has done with their supply. Read the state carefully: still holding is neutral, fully exited on a fresh token is a warning, and transferred out to fresh wallets is the single strongest rug signal DeFade tracks.

tools.name: get_funding_origin
tools.description: Multi-hop tracing of where the money behind this token's key wallets actually came from, tiered by whether the origin is a KYC'd exchange. Use it to test whether several "unrelated" holders share one funding source.

tools.name: get_sybil_cluster
tools.description: Clusters of wallets around one token that behave as a single actor — sized and timed to look like organic demand. Use it alongside get_insider_network when supply looks distributed across many small wallets.

tools.name: get_socials
tools.description: Social presence and links attached to one token contract. Useful for checking whether a project has any verifiable presence behind it.

tools.name: get_token_price
tools.description: Current market data for one token: price, market cap, liquidity and volume. Use it for the market context around a risk verdict, not as a trading feed.

tools.name: compare_holder_overlap
tools.description: Compare two or more tokens and return the wallets that hold several of them. Use it to test whether the same cluster is behind a series of launches — for example a deployer running the same playbook under new tickers.

tools.name: get_trending
tools.description: Tokens currently trending on a given chain. Use it when the user asks what is moving right now rather than about one specific contract; follow up with scan_token before saying anything about safety.

tools.name: check_api_usage
tools.description: Report the calling API key's plan, rate limits and how much of its monthly allowance is left. Use it when a call fails on quota, or when the user asks what their DeFade plan includes.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_token_price · Private data: scan_token, get_rug_score, get_holders, get_whales, get_liquidity, get_bundles, get_bundles_pro, get_snipers, get_insider_network, get_smart_money, get_dev_tracker, get_funding_origin, get_sybil_cluster, get_socials, get_token_price, compare_holder_overlap, get_trending, check_api_usage · Public sink: get_bundles_pro, get_funding_origin · Destructive: scan_token.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_token_price · Private data: scan_token, get_rug_score, get_holders, get_whales, get_liquidity, get_bundles, get_bundles_pro, get_snipers, get_insider_network, get_smart_money, get_dev_tracker, get_funding_origin, get_sybil_cluster, get_socials, get_token_price, compare_holder_overlap, get_trending, check_api_usage · Public sink: get_bundles_pro, get_funding_origin · Destructive: scan_token

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
